오늘 챙겨야 할 해외 이슈

1) 연준 회의: ‘보류하되 매파적 톤’ 가능성 점검 왜 지금 보나: 보도에 따르면 이번 회의에서 금리는 동결 기조가 유력하지만, 최근 물가·소비 지표가 여전히 탄탄하고(헤드라인/핵심 물가 상승, 견조한 소비), AI 수요가 설비투자를 받치는 등 인플레 재가열 우려가 남아 있어 “잠시 멈춤”이 길지 않을 수 있다는 신호가 주목된다. 시장은 10년물 금리 약 5% 부근, 10~12월 추가 인상 가능성을 반영하며 경계 중이고, 임금-물가, 금융여건(장기금리·신용스프레드), 성명서·의장 발언 뉘앙스가 달러/금리/변동성 전반에 파급될 수 있다. 2) ECB·BOJ 동시 점검: 정책 분기와 환율 변동성 왜 지금 보나: 이번 주 ECB와 BOJ도 동결 전망이나, 유럽은 차입비용 부담과 둔화된 성장 사이 균형을, 일본은 물가 전망 상향 여부를 시장이 캐고 있다. 보도에선 엔화가 달러/엔 157부근 약세, 유로도 약세 압력 구간으로 전해졌는데, 정책 분기 고착은 환율 변동을 키워 채권·주식·원자재로 피드백을 낳는다. BOJ의 인플레 전망과 ECB의 12월 가이던스는 캐리 트레이드, 금리차 재확대/축소, 유럽 크레딧 여건에 민감하다. 3) 메가캡 AI 실적: ‘투자(캡엑스) → 수익’ 전환 검증 왜 지금 보나: 알파벳·마이크로소프트·아마존 등 하이퍼스케일러 실적이 집중되며, 데이터센터 중심의 막대한 AI 투자(캡엑스)가 매출·생산성 개선으로 이어지는지 여부가 S&P 500의 이익 시즌 톤과 스타일/섹터 흐름을 좌우한다. 보도는 S&P 500의 3분의 1이 이번 주 발표, AI 지출의 재원조달·마진 압박 논쟁(테크/통신주 변동, 우주·반도체 연쇄 자금조달 사례 언급)까지 시장 베타에 파급될 수 있음을 시사한다. 4) 중동 리스크와 유가: 에너지발 2차 인플레 경계 왜 지금 보나: 최근 브렌트가 6개월 고점 부근까지 치솟은 뒤 완화됐지만, 이란 관련 긴장과 산유국 시설 공격 보도가 이어지며 공급 차질 프리미엄이 남아 있다. 이는 헤드라인 물가와 기대인플레를 통해 연준·ECB의 톤에 영향을 주고, 기업 마진과 운임/항공·화학 등 에너지 민감 업종 변동성을 키울 수 있다. 일부 매체는 금 가격의 방어적 수요도 언급해, ‘리스크오프–인플레’ 동시 노출 구간의 헤지 수요 점검이 필요하다. 5) 장기금리와 금융여건의 동학: ‘이벤트 주간’의 크로스자산 피드백 왜 지금 보나: 보도에 따르면 미국 10년물은 5% 근처, 유럽 일부 국채수익률(프랑스 등)도 상승 압력 속에 있고, 달러는 강보합권이나 엔은 약세, 금은 소폭 강세를 보였다. 이번 주 중앙은행 회의와 메가캡 실적이 겹치며 금리–주식–환율–변동성 간 피드백 루프가 커질 수 있어, 수익률곡선의 추가 상승/안정 여부가 밸류에이션, 달러 유동성, 위험자산 스프레드에 미치는 영향을 동시 관찰할 필요가 있다.

🏦 바젤3 특별 섹션: 채권 평가·변동성 영향

바젤3 최종안·자본규제 1) 핵심 소식: 2026년 3월 19일 ‘ERBA Endgame’ 재제안으로 CET1 영향 축소(연준 직원 추정: 대형은행(Cat I–II) -4.8%, 중형(Cat III–IV) -5.2%, 100억달러 미만 -7.8%). 의무 범위를 Cat I–II로 좁히고, 듀얼 스택을 단일 스택(고급방식)으로 전환, 거래계정 자본을 명시적으로 부과, 일부 범주에서 AOCI 인식 유지. 일정은 2026년 말 최종화 목표. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 위험가중·구조 변화가 은행의 채권 포트폴리오 구성과 회사채 수요를 재조정할 수 있음. 자본 부담이 상대적으로 완화되면(특히 GSIB 서차지·스트레스테스트 상쇄 포함) 딜러·은행의 보유 및 중개 여력에 간접 효과가 생겨 기간 프리미엄·스왑 스프레드에 영향 경로가 열림. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: USD 스왑 스프레드(5년·10년), 프라이머리 딜러의 국채 보유·마켓뎁스(심도) 지표, IG OAS와 은행의 GSIB 서차지·최종안 표결 일정 업데이트. 장기물(TLT)은 기간 프리미엄·중개여력 변화에 더 민감할 수 있어 장기 구간 스프레드/심도 변화를 함께 모니터. 2) 핵심 소식: Reuters — 월가 은행들이 대규모 자본 완화를 포함한 규정 개편(바젤 관련 조정·GSIB 서차지)을 연말까지 마무리하려면 민주당 지지가 필요하다는 정치적 역학. 일부 민주당 인사는 찬성했으나(쿠크, 제퍼슨), 다른 인사(바르 등)는 시스템 리스크 우려로 반대. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 및 (2) 변동성 — 완화 폭·지속가능성에 대한 정치 리스크가 남아 있어 딜러의 대차대조표 운용(중개 한도·재고)과 시장조성 심리에 영향을 줄 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: 규정 확정 전후의 국채 호가스프레드·심도, 스트레스테스트·GSIB 서차지 조정 공지와 스왑 스프레드의 동행성. 불확실성 완화/확대에 따른 중개여력 신호를 체크. 3) 참고 소식: CFTC의 소매 크립토 프레임워크 ANPRM은 바젤3 엔드게임 논의가 병행 중임을 언급하나, 본원적 채권 수급·자본규제 영향은 제한적. - 해당 경로: 직접 해당 없음(맥락 정보). SLR·국채 수요 1) 핵심 소식: Reuters — 유로존 국채 금리 상승으로 은행-주권 ‘둠 루프’ 논쟁 재점화. 유로존 은행의 국채 보유 약 4.3조유로, 국내 편중은 감소했으나 여전히 높음(2026년 중반 41% 수준). HTM 분류 확대로 평가손 인식은 지연, 국채의 무위험 취급·집중한도 개편은 지연, 2027년 다변화 방안 예고. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 금리상승과 자본여력 압박은 은행의 추가 국채·레포 중개 여력을 제약할 수 있어, 글로벌 기간 프리미엄 및 스왑 스프레드에 간접 경로가 존재. (2) 변동성 — 스트레스 시 은행의 흡수자 기능이 약화되면 유동성 저하와 변동성 확대로 이어질 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: 미 재무부 입찰의 간접(해외)·직접(내수) 수요 비중 추세, 유럽 은행 CDS·커브와 미 스왑 스프레드의 동행성, 은행의 HTM/AFS 재분류 관련 공시. 2) 핵심 소식: Reuters — 아시아 중심 사업모델 은행들이 장기금리 상승·물가·FX 변동성으로 자본 스퀴즈. 일본 수익률 상승은 미실현손 확대와 신용등급 하방 압력 가능성을 키움. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 자본비율 압박은 안전자산 추가매수 여지와 레포 중개 여력을 제약할 수 있음. (2) 변동성 — 지역 스트레스가 글로벌 금리·유동성에 파급될 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: TIC 통계의 미 국채에 대한 아시아계 공식/민간 순유입, 레포 스프레드와 특이체 결함률(fails-to-deliver), 지역 은행 실적·자본비율 코멘트. 3) 핵심 소식: 미 재무부 2년물 690억달러 입찰 — 낙찰금리 4.708%, 입찰경쟁률 2.59배, 간접 45.7%로 감소, 직접 41.3%로 사상 최고, 딜러 13.0%. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 수요 주체 구성이 변할 때 딜러 재고·레포 파이낸싱 수요가 달라져 스왑 스프레드·기간 프리미엄 경로에 신호를 줄 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: 단·중기 구간 수요 변화가 IEF에 반영되는지, 입찰 비드투커버·간접 비중의 추세적 변화와 스프레드의 연계. LCR·HQLA·시장 유동성 1) 핵심 소식: BPI — LCR이 저장 유동성(HQLA)만 인정해 과도한 버퍼 유인을 만들며, 중앙은행 할인창구(사전 담보) 기반의 구매 유동성도 인정하자고 제안. 이는 스트레스 시 즉시 유동성 접근을 높이고, 준비금 수요를 낮춰 Fed 대차대조표 축소 여지를 만든다는 논지. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 현행 LCR은 국채·준정부채·준비금 등 HQLA 수요를 구조적으로 지지. 할인창구 인정 시 HQLA 믹스·규모 조정이 가능해 국채·준비금 간 수요 배분이 달라질 수 있음. (2) 변동성 — 구매 유동성 인정은 뱅크런·강제매도 시 유동성 경색을 완화할 여지. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: 은행 HQLA 구성 변화(준비금·국채 비중), ON RRP·준비금 잔액, 할인창구 담보 사전배치 동향과 은행 유동성 공시. 2) 핵심 소식: OFR — 2027년 SEC의 국채 레포 중앙청산 확대 시 SOFR 적격 거래량이 일일 5천억달러 이상 증가 가능. 평균적으로 SOFR 수준 영향은 약 +1bp, 변동성 변화는 제한적이라는 가정(행태 불변). - 해당 경로: (2) 변동성 — 중앙청산은 넷팅·자본효율을 개선해 딜러의 시장조성 여력을 지지할 수 있음. 다만 참가자들이 세그먼트를 재배치하면 금리·스프레드에 소폭 방향성 변화가 생길 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: FICC 스폰서드·DVP 간 물량 이동, SOFR-UST 베이시스, GC-스페셜 스프레드, 국채 시장 호가폭·심도. 3) 핵심 소식: Finadium — 트라이파티·FRM 최적화가 유동성·대차대조표·RWA를 통합 관리하는 핵심 도구로 부상. 레포를 통해 비HQLA를 동원해 HQLA·마진 수요를 충족하고, 참여자·자산군(토큰화 포함) 확대가 진행 중. - 해당 경로: (1) 평가 — 최적화는 은행·딜러의 HQLA 조달과 담보 운용을 효율화해 국채 수요의 운영 기반을 강화. (2) 변동성 — 담보 민첩성이 높아질수록 쇼크 시 마진콜·레버리지 조정의 경직성이 완화되어 유동성 고갈 위험을 줄일 수 있음. - TLT/IEF에서 볼 것: 트라이파티 잔액·담보 적격성 변경, 담보 재사용률, 디지털/토큰화 담보 시범사업의 체결·스프레드 영향. 요약 최근 규제 흐름은 위험가중·유동성 프레임을 재설계해 은행의 대차대조표 제약을 조정하려는 방향과, 레포 인프라·담보 운용을 고도화해 시장조성의 내구성을 높이려는 방향이 병행되고 있다. 이는 구조적 수요(HQLA)와 중개여력(레버리지·청산·담보 최적화)의 균형에 따라 국채 유동성의 탄력성이 달라질 수 있음을 시사하며, 충격 시 변동성의 크기와 지속성을 좌우할 수 있다.

Basel III Endgame Re-Proposal Explained: What ERBA Changes
Mirai RiskTech · 2026-10-21T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - The 2023 US Basel III endgame proposal would have raised CET1 requirements for affected holding companies by about 16%. - A March 19, 2026 re-proposal (ERBA Endgame) cuts those increases: on Fed staff estimates, by 4.8% for Categories I–II, 5.2% for Categories III–IV, and 7.8% for banks below $100 billion. - Key changes in the re-proposal: - Mandatory scope narrowed to Categories I–II; Categories III–IV can opt in with four quarters’ notice under the same capital definitions (including AOCI). Market risk framework applies to Category I–II and larger trading firms. - The approach shifts from a dual stack to a single stack: for Category I–II, standardized risk-weighted approach is removed; firms compute one set of risk-based ratios using advanced approaches only. - ERBA design adjustments respond to the 2023 proposal’s issues: single risk-based framework, opposite net effect due to compensating factors like the GSIB surcharge and stress tests. - Capital impact details (Fed staff estimates in a board memo, March 19, 2026): - Categories I–II: Basel III (ERBA) NPR +1.4% (net effect negative due to other components), G-SIB surcharge NPR negative, standardized approach risks negative, AOCI recognition positive for some groups, stress test changes broadly negative or mixed. - Total CET1 impact (aggregate): Categories I–II -4.8%, Categories III–IV -5.2%, Below $100bn -7.8%. - Comparison: 2023 proposal would have raised CET1 by about +16% (Categories I–II for larger banks). - Status and timeline: - The three March 2026 NPRs were open for comment until mid-2026; agencies aimed for a year-end 2026 final rule, with a vote anticipated in December 2026. - The re-proposal is not a softening of the prior plan; it retools scope, structure (single stack), and risk charges in response to previous outcomes. - Additional notes: - The ERBA framework explicitly adds capital for trading books and keeps most AOCI recognition for Categories III–IV, reflecting SVB-related concerns. - An August 2023 long-term debt proposal for large non-G-SIBs remains separate and not yet finalized. Liquidity Regulations and the Discount Window: Restoring a Balance Between Stored and Purchased Liquidity - Bank Policy Institute
Will Bonner · 2026-10-23T18:46:27.000Z

Summary: - The Basel Liquidity Coverage Ratio (LCR) requires banks to hold enough high-quality liquid assets (HQLA) to cover 30-day net cash outflows, with LCR ≥ 100%. Current rules only count stored liquidity (HQLA) and do not recognize purchased liquidity from the central bank’s discount window. - Stored liquidity is often inefficient (the “last taxi problem”): even with a projected outflow, banks must hold HQLA against all deposits, leaving usable liquidity limited when runs occur and compelling banks to maintain excess buffers that reduce lending to the real economy. - The piece argues for recognizing purchased liquidity (e.g., discount window borrowing against pre-positioned collateral) as part of HQLA. This would: - Provide immediate access to liquidity during stress. - Allow banks to extend more credit to the real economy without violating the LCR. - Potentially reduce the demand for central bank reserves driven by liquidity regulations and enable a smaller Fed balance sheet. - Overall finding: including discount-window borrowing capacity as HQLA mitigates LCR distortions, supports greater credit provision during crises, and aligns regulatory metrics with the central bank’s lender-of-last-resort role.

Gold and Midterms: Is this time different? | Post by Juan Carlos Artigas | Insights | World Gold Council
Juan Carlos Artigas · 2026-10-22T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: The article from the World Gold Council examines how the 2026 US midterm outcomes could influence gold prices through macro policy channels rather than election day results alone. Prediction markets favor Democratic control of both chambers, which could affect fiscal policy, war funding, AI regulation, and executive powers—all of which interact with gold’s price dynamics. Key macro drivers highlighted: - Fiscal policy: Democratic control could restrain deficit-spending, easing inflation risks and reducing Treasuries’ safety-driven demand for a stronger dollar. If deficits widen, gold could be supported; contracting deficits could weigh on gold. - War funding: Potential de-escalation of conflicts under Democratic control could lower energy prices and inflation expectations, softening yields and the dollar, but still generally remain supportive of gold; a geopolitical premium may reduce. - AI regulation: Possible tighter AI regulation or slower hyperscale spending under Democratic control could weaken tech equities and growth, supporting a wealth-driven shift toward gold as a safe asset. - Executive/emergency powers: Greater congressional constraints might increase reliance on executive actions, creating policy uncertainty and higher geopolitical risk premia, which could bolster gold demand. Implications if Republicans gain control: - The report notes mixed effects but suggests continued support for gold from non-US investors due to ongoing global risk sentiment and the potential for persistent geopolitical tensions. Bottom line: Gold price outlook is driven more by evolving macro-fiscal policy, inflation expectations, energy prices, equity market dynamics, and geopolitical risk—not election-day outcomes. In the current geoeconomic environment, gold could remain supported by policy uncertainty and risk premia, though specific policy shifts (deficit trajectories, war funding, AI regulation) will shape the degree of support.

Storage rose modestly to 3,567 Bcf (week ended Oct 9). - LNG export role: US LNG exports rising (expected ~17.6 Bcf/d in 2026; ~18.6 Bcf/d in 2027) support prices at higher levels if demand remains strong, with LNG flows potentially exceeding 20 Bcf/d by year-end per Enverus. - European gas: Much higher, about $29.50/MMBtu (≈€89.8/MWh) due to low storage (74% vs. five-year 86%) and Middle East supply risk, roughly 9.5x Henry Hub price. - AI/data-center demand: Long-run driver of gas demand, with Wood Mackenzie estimating ~17 Bcf/d of incremental demand by mid-2030s, potentially pushing Henry Hub higher later (some forecasts near $5 by 2035). In the near term, data-center demand has not yet moved US prices noticeably; weather and LNG/export dynamics dominate. - What to watch: Weekly EIA storage reports, the November 10 outlook, and Europe’s storage trajectory. Watch for potential price spikes from cold weather or LNG disruption; longer-term risk hinges on data-center load growth and LNG export capacity. Key takeaway for macro analysts: Near-term US gas markets remain supply- and weather-driven with modest price upside from LNG exports; long-run price potential rises if AI/data-center demand accelerates, but current prices still reflect a balance of production growth and export flows. European prices remain detached high due to storage risk and regional supply constraints.

Arable Market Report – 26 October 2026 | AHDB
ahdb.org.uk · 2026-10-26T16:40:34.000Z

Summary: - UK feed wheat: Nov-2026 at £193.75/t, down £11.25/t week-on-week. Prices sit below the 20-day moving average with weakened momentum and RSI at 27, indicating near-term downside and oversold conditions. - Market drivers: Global grain prices fell due to improving supply prospects, US harvest progress, and selective Black Sea disruption plus crude oil firmness. Russia–Ukraine peace-talk hopes also pressured prices. - Nearby Chicago wheat and maize fell (6.5% and 3.9% respectively); Paris milling wheat down ~4%. - US weather improved fieldwork and winter wheat planting; dry spells ahead unlikely to halt progress, suggesting continued downward price pressure as large 2026 crop harvest nears. - Black Sea developments remain pivotal: Russia expanding export routes (Baltic Sea) and higher export forecasts for October (2.8 Mt from 2.5 Mt prior). - Oilseeds: Prices weakened on better US harvest conditions and relief from Black Sea tensions, though late-week crude oil gains and strong export sales supported soybeans. May-2027 futures: Chicago soybeans -0.6%, Paris rapeseed -0.9%, Winnipeg canola -1.7%. - Geopolitics and supply: Negotiations among Ukraine, Russia, and the US ongoing with potential November talks in Abu Dhabi; continued conflict risks to Black Sea exports and commodity prices. - UK supply outlook (AHDB): 2026/27 wheat and barley supply/demand projections indicate tighter Wheat balance due to lower opening stocks despite higher production; barley faces a very tight balance due to lower production (lowest since 2012/13). Imports likely important for wheat; barley at elevated tightness. Bottom line: The Arable market is characterized by near-term downside pressure for cereals amid improving US harvest conditions and ample global supply prospects, tempered by geopolitical tensions that could support certain oilseed and grain prices depending on Black Sea export developments. The UK 2026/27 balance sheets suggest tighter Wheat and especially Barley supply, increasing import reliance for Wheat.

Monthly Grain Market Outlook | Weekly Crop Update
sites.udel.edu · 2026-10-20T00:00:00.000Z

Summary: - The Monthly Grain Market Outlook notes that profitability is tight as harvest continues, with high production costs pressuring enterprise budgets. Marketing decisions are crucial as grain futures have declined recently, making it harder to lock in favorable prices. - For those with stored grain, it may be more profitable to take the price discounts rather than dry and store yourself, depending on costs and marketing price points. - Corn: Futures spiked in September but retreated in October after the Trump-Xi Summit disappointment and a bearish USDA quarterly stocks report (beginning stocks raised to about 2.095 billion bu). The October WASDE projects a large US corn crop (potentially second-largest on record). Exports rose in the report, but a stronger US dollar remains a headwind. Near-term sentiment is cautious with potential upside if marketing positions were taken previously. - Soybeans: Prices cooled after September highs. Tariff announcements post-summit were negative for futures, though Chinese state buyers did purchase US soybeans (first since the summit). US soybean production was robust, with an increased yield projection (53.1 bu/acre from 52.8). The quarterly stocks declined modestly (315 million bu), not producing a strong bullish impact. More planted acres (5.7 million more) support potential supply and price dynamics. - Wheat: Futures softened with mixed expectations for renewed demand; export activity has not strengthened as hoped despite initial optimism for Wheat export opportunities from China. - Overall market context: The period’s price action reflects a global supply/demand balance with tight world supplies in some areas but a stronger US dollar and larger-than-expected US crops weighing on prices. Producers should monitor WASDE updates, ethanol/exports data, and the evolving marketing environment; revisiting budgets and deciding on storage vs. sale now could improve profitability as harvest continues. If you want, I can tailor this to a specific grain (corn, soybeans, wheat) or focus on strategy guidance (marketing price points, discounts vs. drying costs) based on your production mix.

ADM Investor Services Agricultural Market View (Oct 21, 2026) - Grain and oilseed broadly weaker yet some intra-day bounce: - Corn and soy complex: prices down in a volatile session; beans off $0.03–$0.09, meal down $1–$3, oil down 70–80 points. Nov-26 beans hit a fresh 2-month low; Dec-26 oil at a 3½-month low before rebound. Spreads firmed for beans/meal; oil spreads mixed. - Wheat: Dec-26 CGO, KC, and MIAX contracts down $0.15–$0.18; Wheat led declines on a softer macro/war-premium backdrop tied to Ukraine peace-talk developments. - Key support and technicals: - Soybeans: Fibonacci support at $12.29 and 100-day MA at $12.27¼ for Dec-26. - Wheat: fund/positioning near-term with large net-short in CGO wheat (43k–50k contracts), potential for further volatility. - Supplies, demand, and margins: - Beef/cattle: COF report expected; cattle inventories around 11.441 million head as of Oct 1; placements down ~8.3%, marketing down ~7.3%. - Ethanol/energy: ethanol production up to 322 million gallons last week; margins remain firm as energy prices stay high and corn prices slide; 685 million bushels of corn used in MY-to-date production (annualized pace ~5.43 billion bu, below USDA forecast). - Soy/meal/oil: USDA flash sales of soybeans to China (134k MT) and Spain (165k MT); China purchases near 17.5 MMT; US Gulf prices persist $.20–$.30 below Brazilian offers into year-end; Brazil Oct exports expected at 6.4 MMT (vs 6.54 MMT LY). - Outlook and next catalysts: - For a meaningful bounce, need improved demand or a more threatening SA forecast. - Tomorrow’s export sales expected: 65–110 million bu of beans, 250–650k tons meal, 0–10k tons oil. - US harvest progress: likely 80%+ complete by weekend; showers in the Plains may affect development but dry Midwest supports harvest pace. - Global context: Ukraine war risk premiums easing; SovEcon lowers Ukraine grain exports further, highlighting ongoing global supply/demand sensitivity. Bottom line: Near-term downside pressure across grains with some bounce potential on improving demand signals (and sustained tight fundamentals in corn/beans vs. robust biofuel demand). Watch export sales, harvest progress, and evolving geopolitical factors (Ukraine/Black Sea security) for momentum shifts.

AGS WEEK AHEAD: Brazilian Real in Focus as Dollar-Denominated Ags Fall
www.marketwatch.com · 2026-10-26T00:00:00.000Z

Ags Week Ahead (Oct 26–30) overview: The Brazilian real weakened after Lula’s election win, boosting Brazil’s export competitiveness for coffee, sugar, and soybeans but sparking potential political uncertainty if challenger challenges results. Key points: - Market driver: A softer real improves Brazil exporters’ local revenue and farmer selling against global prices. - Relevant commodities: Soybeans, coffee, and sugar led declines after the election; cocoa also fell. - Soybeans: ~1.55% lower to $12.37/bushel. - Coffee: -2.75% to $2.99/lb. - Sugar: -6.5% to 18.92 cents/lb; noted as vulnerable due to speculative long positions. - Cocoa: -1.75% to $5,496/ton. - Wheat: -1.4% to $6.16/bushel. - Corn: -0.4% to $4.54/bushel. - Feedstock/crop expectations: U.S. corn production expectations dampen sentiment; favorable weather in the U.S. corn belt and South America supports near-term harvests and planting. - Policy/monetary influence: The Federal Reserve is expected to hold rates; hawkish hints could strengthen the dollar and weigh on ags. Market jitters around Lula’s victory and potential challenge add risk. - Investor behavior: CFTC data showed a retreat by speculators in ags; sugar previously had crowded long bets. Bottom line: Near-term macro and political risk (Brazilian election uncertainty) interacts with favorable weather and expected Fed hold. The weaker real supports Brazilian exports long term, but immediate price pressure is evident across soy, coffee, sugar, and other grains amid mixed speculative positioning and potential dollar strength. Consider monitoring: Brazilian real movements, election developments, Fed stance, and U.S. crop-weather updates for corn/soybeans.

Summary: Agricultural commodities outlook (corn, soybeans, winter wheat) - Corn: Prices pulled back after a brief rally; Dec corn closed above August low signaling possible bottoming action, but near-term weakness persists due to favorable harvest weather. Mark Schultz suggests a potential short-term bottom with oversold conditions, likely leading to a bounce, followed by hedge pressure for 5–10 days as harvest progresses toward 70% completion. - Soybeans: Rebounded from earlier lows aided by strong weekly exports, including significant purchase by China (roughly 80 million bushels in the latest week, plus a flash sale). Export momentum and easing hedge pressure from harvest wrapping up support the bounce. Funds had been net long; liquidation may be finishing and demand from China and crushers improving basis levels. - Winter wheat: New move to fresh lows, trading below the 200-day moving average amid poor weekly exports (~8.8 million bu) and reduced YTD sales. War/ weather premium largely unwound; outlook bearish longer term. Rains in Plains boosted moisture, raising expectations of higher next-year acreage (+3–4 million), contributing to softer near-term wheat prices. Overall takeaway: Corn appears near a potential short-term bottom with oversold conditions and seasonal tendencies; soybeans are showing strength on robust export demand from China and improving basis as harvest winds down; winter wheat remains weak on poor export pace and expectations of higher future acreage, dampening the broader grains complex.
